findings.evidence: Authenticated callers can execute set_secondary_password(text). Its current body checks auth.uid and password length, then INSERT ON CONFLICT UPDATE replaces an existing password hash and resets failed-attempt/lock fields. It requires no previous password, primary reauthentication proof, or live auth.sessions row.
findings.impact: A valid primary bearer token can replace its own account's secondary credential directly; the UI's verification is not an enforceable server replacement boundary. This does not demonstrate an unauthenticated or different-user write.
findings.recommendation: Reuse staged operation-proof protocol, close legacy overwrite when an equivalent usable recovery path is ready, and cover live-session and OAuth-only users before activation.

findings.evidence: reauthentication_capabilities, issue_reauthentication_proof, replace_secondary_password_with_proof, and both private proof/rollout tables are absent. reauthenticate-operation is absent from deployed Edge names.
findings.impact: Staged client code falls back on PGRST202; source implementation and prior isolated tests are not a deployed server guarantee.
findings.recommendation: Review and reuse staged SQL/Edge/client artifacts; do not invent a second proof scheme or mark a nonexistent backend merely OFF.

findings.evidence: verify_secondary_password(text) returns boolean and updates only credential failure counters. New admin require_manager validates live actor/session, company role and feature, but consumes no secondary-success receipt.
findings.impact: SecondaryProtectedPage guards app navigation; directly calling an authenticated management RPC does not prove that secondary authentication occurred.
findings.recommendation: Introduce a server-issued current-session/action/target-bound step-up receipt before describing the management action as server-enforced second authentication. Native Face ID alone is not server proof.

findings.evidence: SecondaryPasswordPrimaryVerifier compares currentUser().id at start and finish. The reset page stores an actor ID after verification but does not subscribe to auth history or bind that result to session_id through save.
findings.impact: An A->B->A or same-actor different-session transition can satisfy final actor equality. Server proof mode would independently constrain SID, but that mode is not deployed.
findings.recommendation: Capture session identity plus auth-event history from verification through save; preserve same-session token refresh rules and invalidate on logout/other session. Coordinate exclusive file ownership before editing.

findings.evidence: Current force_manage_attendance body deletes daily_report_workers then inserts replacement rows without mentioning company_allowance_selections or company_allowance_legacy_labels. The before_state audit preserves old rows, but the current row is not reconstructed from those typed values.
findings.impact: An unrelated force upsert can remove registered selection identity/current-row metadata while retaining only free allowance_names. An audit copy is not current financial-source preservation.
findings.recommendation: Parent-owned fix must preserve unchanged typed values exactly, keep free names separate, validate explicit registered changes by ID/version/unit, and add one focused Native unrelated-edit preservation regression.

findings.evidence: Current security advisor reports auth_leaked_password_protection disabled.
findings.impact: Password-service breach-list defense is not enabled; this says nothing about strength or exposure of a specific user's password.
findings.recommendation: Review current Auth settings and plan eligibility, then make a concrete reviewed configuration change. Do not alter Google/Apple/Face ID identities or lock OAuth-only recovery.
